theater: 巴士拉以南鹽沼與底格里斯下游

battle.name: 張格爾之亂
battle.theater: 巴士拉以南鹽沼與底格里斯下游
battle.brief: 戰爭列表把張格爾之亂編在一八二〇至一八二七年；阿拉伯史料中的津芝叛亂起於八六九年、終於八八三年，戰場在巴士拉以南鹽沼與底格里斯下游。叛軍以沼澤游擊、水網舟隊與夜襲拖住阿拔斯軍隊十四年，最後在穆赫塔拉被圍城攻破。卡面的火繩槍是十六世紀西班牙的裝備，比此役晚六百餘年，未見於戰場。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 交戰雙方都在阿拔斯王朝的疆域之內，衝突的舞台是伊拉克南部、巴士拉以南大片鹽沼與底格里斯下游的運河水網。朝廷一方自八六一年起陷於薩邁拉無政府狀態，哈里發接連更替，欠餉的軍隊多次兵變，中央財政近乎破產，總督在自己的轄區內幾乎不受節制；真正主持南部戰役的是哈里發之弟、攝政穆瓦法克，他在巴格達調度軍費、任命主將，前線部隊則由巴士拉與瓦西特兩省總督就地籌措。政府軍的組成是當年伊拉克軍團的標準搭配：土庫斯系奴兵騎兵充當前鋒，伊拉克步兵以弓手與長槍手為主，攻城時另調工程隊、撞槌、投石機與火油投射器，阿拉伯部族騎兵隨軍作戰，擔任追擊與斷糧；軍費靠國庫撥款與薩瓦德鹽沼農業區的地稅，而那片被開墾的沼澤正是雙方爭奪的核心。起義一方沒有單一血緣：主體是被販入伊拉克的東非黑奴及其受釋者，外圍有巴士拉城內的工匠、依附豪門的半自由民、小農與周邊貝都因部落；首領阿里·本·穆罕默德自稱先知與阿里後裔，在沼澤中的穆赫塔拉建都，自行徵稅、鑄幣，並在運河上組織舟隊，把一場奴工暴動變成有行政、有財政的地方政權。戰爭列表所採的一八二〇至一八二七年，則落在鄂托曼統治下南部沼澤再度騷動的年代；那一段只留下零星記載，交戰一方是省府軍隊與受徵召的部族騎兵，另一方是拒絕新稅與駐軍的沼澤居民及其盟友，詳細編制諸說並存，難以確指。
countriesEn: Both sides of this conflict lay inside the territory of the Abbasid Caliphate, and the stage was southern Iraq, in the wide salt marshes south of Basra and the canal network of the lower Tigris. On the court side the centre had been paralysed since 861 by the Anarchy at Samarra: caliphs succeeded one another in quick succession, unpaid troops mutinied again and again, the treasury came close to bankruptcy, tax revenue leaked away, and governors were left almost unsupervised in their own provinces. The man who actually directed the southern war was the caliph's brother and regent al-Muwaffaq, who ran the campaign from Baghdad, raised the money and appointed the commanders, while the troops in the field were levied locally by the governors of Basra and Wasit. The government army was the standard Iraqi mix of the era: Turkish slave cavalry in front, Iraqi infantry whose main weapons were the bow and the spear, and for the sieges engineers, battering rams, stone-throwing engines and naphtha projectors, with Arab tribal cavalry riding along and taking over pursuit and the cutting of supplies. The war was paid for out of the treasury and out of the land tax of the Sawad salt-marsh plantations, and those reclaimed marshes were precisely the ground the two sides fought over. The rebel side had no single ethnic identity: its core was the Zanj, enslaved and freed East Africans carried in through the Indian Ocean trade, ringed by craftsmen in Basra, half-freed dependants of great families, tenant peasants and a few Bedouin groups around the city. Their commander Ali ibn Muhammad proclaimed himself a prophet and a descendant of Ali, made his capital at al-Mukhtarah in the marshes south of Basra, levied taxes, struck his own coin, and organised a boat force on the canals, turning what had begun as a slave rising into a regional power with its own administration and finances. The 1820 to 1827 span used by the war list falls in the years when the southern marshes of Ottoman Iraq stirred again; only scattered notices survive for that period. On one side stood provincial troops and tribal cavalry called up to serve, on the other the marsh dwellers who refused new taxes and the stationing of garrisons, and the detailed order of battle varies from source to source and cannot be fixed with certainty.
people: 這場起義留下姓名的核心人物只有一位。編年史記載，阿里·本·穆罕默德出生在波斯賴伊附近，祖父一支屬阿卜杜·蓋斯部族，早年在薩邁拉依附穆塔西爾的權貴奴僕；八六三年他前往巴林，偽裝什葉派起事並募集支持，失敗後轉到巴士拉，利用城內比比利耶與薩德耶兩派的衝突尋找機會，事敗被地方當局逮捕送抵瓦西特，脫身後在巴格達停留一年，並以扎伊迪派血統自居；八六九年返回巴士拉沼澤，在黑奴群體中宣講解放與財富分配，逐步聚起人馬，自稱津芝之主，同時保留阿里後裔的說法，並借用哈瓦利吉派那套「最合格者當統治」的平等主張作為號召。哈里發穆塔米德受制於欠餉的軍人與崩潰的財政，未能提供可靠支援；攝政穆瓦法克才是實際主帥，他於八七九年先遣次子阿布·阿爾·阿巴斯率主力進軍，翌年親赴前線，改以掃蕩與招撫並行的手段進攻。哈里發軍方面的將領名見於編年史但譯名互有出入，據記載最後主持圍城與追捕的是穆罕默德·伊本·伊薩·朱魯迪，而軍費與任命由巴格達的宰相一系掌管；叛軍內部則有人以出賣首領換取寬免，成為攻城之後最關鍵的一環，也是圍城得以收束的心理缺口。
peopleEn: Only one figure in this rising left a name in the sources. The chronicles describe Ali ibn Muhammad as born near Rayy in Persia, his paternal line belonging to the tribe of Abd al-Qays, and he spent part of his youth in Samarra among the powerful dependants of Caliph al-Muntasir. In 863 he went to Bahrayn in eastern Arabia, posed as a Shiite and raised support, and after that rising collapsed he moved to Basra, where he tried to exploit the fighting between the city's Bilaliyyah and Sa'diyyah factions. Having failed he was seized by the provincial authorities and sent to Wasit, escaped, and spent a year in Baghdad, where he claimed descent from the grandson of Zayd ibn Ali and called himself a Zaydi. When factional strife broke out in Basra again in 869 he returned, began moving among the black slaves working the marshes, promised them freedom and a share of wealth, and gradually built a following, calling himself the Chief of the Zanj. He kept up the pretension of Alid descent while borrowing the egalitarian doctrine of the Kharijites, that the most qualified man ought to rule even if he is a slave, and that doctrine gave the rising a cause that reached past the personal circumstances of its adherents. Caliph al-Mu'tamid, himself constrained by unpaid soldiers and a ruined treasury, could not be relied upon. The real commander was the regent al-Muwaffaq, who sent his son Abu al-'Abbas with the main force in 879 and joined the offensive in person the following year, combining sweeps through the countryside with offers of generous terms to those who surrendered. The names of the caliphal commanders appear in the chronicles in conflicting transliterations; the general credited with the final siege and the pursuit is Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi, while appointments and finance were handled in Baghdad by the vizierate. Inside the rebel camp there were men ready to betray their own leader in exchange for mercy, and that willingness proved to be the decisive gap in the siege and the reason it could be closed.
kits: 卡面兵器是火繩槍，這件武器與本卡的戰爭沒有戰場上的交集，必須先講清楚。火繩槍是十五、十六世紀的歐洲產物，十六世紀的西班牙把它裝在方陣的火槍手手上：一條緩慢燃燒的引線夾在叉架上，射手先點火、備好火繩，再把火繩拉過擊發機構點燃火藥，裝藥、引火、瞄準、排成一線，一整套動作做完才算射擊，所以它要點火、要瞄、要排隊，方陣把這些弱點變成整齊的彈幕。可此役的實際年月遠在火繩槍之前：就算取戰爭列表所採的一八二〇年代，那時的鄂托曼軍隊早已改用燧發步槍與長管燧槍，火繩槍只剩少量舊式短槍留在守備舊堡的庫房裡。回到史載的那一次起事，戰場上根本沒有火藥武器：伊斯蘭世界最早的手持火器也要到十二、十三世紀才出現，火繩槍的祖型更在其後。叛軍實際使用的是複合弓、直刃阿拉伯劍、長矛與標槍、木框蒙皮圓盾、鐵盔或銅盔，以及用皮條鉚接的鑲片甲；營寨以蘆葦與泥牆搭建，一經火攻即焚，所以攻城方總是直接縱火。哈里發軍是重騎加步兵的標準組合，攻城配備工程梯、撞槌與投石機，雙方都用過火油投射器與火罐，攻擊沼澤棚寨時尤其倚重。武器來源有繳獲、劫掠政府軍哨站與自造三路，叛軍自己也養著冶鐵與造箭的匠人。
kitsEn: The card shows a matchlock musket, and that weapon has no battlefield presence in the war on this card, so the point has to be made plainly. The matchlock is a European weapon of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, and in sixteenth-century Spain it was put into the hands of the arquebusiers of the square: a slowly burning cord held in a forked rest, the match lit and prepared in advance, then drawn across the mechanism to fire the charge, while loading, priming, aiming and standing in rank were all carried out first, so that the whole sequence had to be completed before a shot was possible. It needed light, it needed aim and it needed rank, and the square turned those weaknesses into an orderly volley. But the fighting recorded under this name long predates the matchlock: even taking the 1820s span used by the war list, Ottoman troops had long since moved to flintlock muskets and long-barrelled guns, and the matchlock survived only as a few old short pieces left in the stores of obsolete fortresses. Return to the rising as the chronicles record it, and there was no gunpowder weapon on the battlefield at all: the earliest hand-held gunpowder weapons in the Islamic world appear only in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, and the ancestors of the matchlock came later still. What the insurgents actually used were composite bows, straight Arab swords, spears and javelins, wooden-framed hides covered round shields, iron or bronze helmets, and lamellar armour of leather thongs and riveted plates. Their camps were built of reeds and mud plaster and burned readily, so an assault almost always ended in fire. The caliphal army was the usual combination of heavy cavalry and infantry, with scaling ladders, rams and stone-throwing engines for the sieges; both sides used naphtha projectors and fire-pots, and fire was especially important against the reed-built strongholds in the marshes. Weapons came from captures, from raids on government posts and from their own smiths, and the rebels kept metalworkers and arrow-makers busy.
tactics: 起義初期，叛軍人數極少，靠分散在沼澤邊緣的小隊維持：夜襲政府軍巡邏、驛站與小營，奪取武器、馬匹、糧食和俘虜，救出同族，再把帶不走的物資一把火燒掉以延緩追擊；取得立足之後築起沼澤堡壘，以平底小艇在運河上編成一支分隊，避免與正規騎兵正面交鋒，並在控制區徵稅鑄幣，把游擊變成有財源的地方統治。政府軍初期屢戰屢敗，原因不在裝備而在情報與補給：遠征隊一旦離開主要道路、深入沼澤，分隊與哨站之間便失去聯絡，被分割殲滅；官軍能依靠的補給點只有巴士拉與瓦西特兩處，前線一拉長，軍糧與箭矢就接不上。八七〇至八七六年間雙方在薩瓦德與胡威斯反覆拉鋸，起義軍攻佔城鎮、擴張稅源，官軍則退守要邑重建補給線。八七九年起政府轉守為攻，集結兵力掃清伊拉克與胡威斯，把叛軍逐回首都穆赫塔拉；八八一年二月起實施長期圍城，同時以優厚條件招撫，瓦解叛軍內部的依附關係，並曾嘗試築壩填塞水道、切斷叛軍在沼澤中的往來。八月城破，殘部在沼澤中被追捕，首腦被自己人出賣。一八二〇年代那一線的記載則只到「討伐與安撫並用」的層次：省府一方面出兵，另一方面用特赦與減稅換取沼澤部族的順從，細節無從確指。
tacticsEn: In its first phase the rising was kept alive by very small detachments dispersed along the edge of the marshes. They struck government patrols, relay stations and small camps at night, took weapons, horses, food and prisoners, freed their own people, and burned what they could not carry away so as to delay the counter-attack. Once established they raised fortresses in the marsh, formed a flotilla of flat-bottomed boats to work the canals, avoided meeting regular cavalry in the open, and in the areas they held they levied taxes and struck coin, turning raiding into a local government with its own revenue. The government's early defeats were not caused by inferior equipment but by poor intelligence and supply: once an expeditionary column left the main tracks and pushed into the marsh, its detachments and posts lost contact with one another and were destroyed piecemeal. The only fixed supply points the government had were Basra and Wasit, and once the front was stretched, food and arrows stopped arriving. Between 870 and 876 the two sides traded the ground repeatedly across the Sawad and al-Ahwaz, the rebels taking towns and widening their tax base while the government fell back on the fortified towns and rebuilt its lines of supply. From 879 the government took the initiative, massed troops to clear Iraq and al-Ahwaz and drove the rebels back towards their capital al-Mukhtarah. A long siege opened in February 881, run together with generous offers of pardon that broke the personal ties holding the rebel side together, and the besiegers are also credited with attempts to dam and fill the waterways in order to cut the rebels' movements across the marsh. The town fell in August, the survivors were hunted through the marshes, and the leader was betrayed by one of his own. For the 1820s thread the record only reaches the level of pursuit and accommodation used together: the provincial government raised troops on one side and on the other offered amnesty and reduced dues to win the marsh tribes over, and the details cannot be pinned down.
data: 本站戰爭列表把此條目編在一八二〇至一八二七年；這組年份落在鄂托曼統治下南部沼澤反覆騷動的年代，相關記載只留下片段，可核實的數字極少，能確認的只有起訖的年分，以及那幾年南部沼澤持續有武裝衝突。至於史冊中以「張格爾之亂」為名、記載最完整的那一次起事，時序反而清楚：起於八六九年九月，終於八八三年八月，前後約十四年；穆赫塔拉的長期圍城自八八一年二月起算，約兩年半；同年十一月三十日阿布·阿爾·阿巴斯進入巴格達舉行凱旋。地理上，叛軍最遠曾推進到巴士拉與瓦西特之間的沼澤，並沿底格里斯河向西北逼近，據記載一度距巴格達約五十英里、八十餘公里；作戰核心在巴士拉以南的鹽沼與運河地帶。兵力方面，政府先後投入多支大軍，各書記載的數目互有出入，可靠的說法是叛軍在高峰期達數萬人量級，政府軍則是當年裝備最齊整的一批部隊；九世紀史家如馬蘇迪把叛軍寫成極大的數目，現代學者多視為誇大之辭。死傷人數在數萬量級，圍城之後投降與被擄者數以萬計，繳獲與徵收的財富只有概括敘述，沒有可核的數字。
dataEn: The war list on this site dates the entry to 1820 to 1827. Those years fall in a period of repeated unrest in the southern marshes under Ottoman rule, and the record for them survives only in fragments, with very little that can be verified: the span of the years, and the fact that armed conflict was taking place in the southern marshes through them. The best documented rising that carries the name Zanj rebellion has a firmer chronology: it opened in September 869 and ended in August 883, about fourteen years in all; the long siege of al-Mukhtarah ran from February 881, roughly two and a half years; and on 30 November 883 Abu al-'Abbas entered Baghdad and held a victory parade. Geographically the rebels reached their furthest extent in the marshes between Basra and Wasit and then pushed north-west along the Tigris, coming at one point to within about fifty miles, some eighty kilometres, of Baghdad; the fighting core lay in the salt marshes and canal network south of Basra. On numbers of troops, the government committed several large armies in turn and the figures given in different books disagree, so the safe statement is that the rebels reached a peak in the tens of thousands while the government fielded the best equipped forces of the year; the ninth-century historian al-Mas'udi wrote the rebel numbers up to an enormous figure, which modern scholars generally treat as gross exaggeration. Losses are placed in the tens of thousands, the numbers who surrendered or were taken after the siege ran to many thousands, and the seizures and collected revenue of the rebels survive only as general statements with no figures that can be checked.
cause: 起事有兩條根子。其一是薩瓦德鹽沼農業區的開墾依賴大量勞力，東非奴隸被集中在鹽沼挖渠清淤的工作營，待遇惡劣，早在六八九年到六九〇年、以及六九四年已有兩次較早的反抗，只是規模小而迅速被壓下。其二是阿拔斯中央在八六一年之後陷入薩邁拉無政府狀態：哈里發接連更替，欠餉的軍隊多次兵變，中央財政近乎破產，稅收流失，總督在自己的轄區內幾乎不受節制，中央一時無力向南調兵。巴士拉城內兩派爭鬥讓阿里·本·穆罕默德找到可乘之機，他先在巴林起事失敗，之後轉入沼澤，向黑奴許諾自由與財富，把一個長年在鹽沼裡勞作的群體變成有共同訴求的軍隊；其主張兼有宗教改革與奴隸解放，用的正是哈瓦利吉派「最合格者當統治」的說法，這讓起事有了超越個人身分的號召力。同時期薩法里王朝的雅庫布·伊本·萊斯向胡威斯推進，抽走中央可以調動的兵力，讓南部戰局更加空虛。若就戰爭列表所採的一八二〇年代而言，起因可查的只有一點：鄂托曼時期南部沼澤的稅賦與駐軍同樣是衝突的來源，沼澤居民拒絕新的徵斂，而省府在對波斯方向用兵之餘可供調度的部隊有限；具體首謀者與經過，諸說並存，無可靠記載可引。
causeEn: The rising had two roots. The first was the working of the Sawad salt-marsh plantations, which needed a large labour force: East African slaves were herded into work camps in the marshes to dig canals and clear silt, treated badly, and there had already been two earlier risings, in 689 to 690 and in 694, both small and quickly crushed. The second was that the Abbasid centre had fallen into the Anarchy at Samarra after 861: caliphs changing rapidly, unpaid troops mutinying more than once, the treasury close to bankruptcy, tax revenue leaking away, governors left almost entirely to their own devices in their provinces, and the centre in no position to send troops south. The factional fighting inside Basra gave Ali ibn Muhammad his opening; after his failed rising in Bahrayn he turned to the marshes and promised the black slaves freedom and wealth, turning a population labouring for years in the salt flats into an army with a common cause. His message joined religious reform to the emancipation of slaves, and it borrowed the Kharijite claim that the most qualified man ought to rule, which gave the revolt a call reaching beyond the personal standing of its adherents. At the same time the advance of Ya'qub ibn al-Layth of the Saffarids into al-Ahwaz drew off troops the government might otherwise have sent, leaving the southern theatre even thinner. As for the 1820s span used by the war list, only one cause can be traced with confidence: under Ottoman rule the tax burden and the stationing of garrisons in the southern marshes were likewise a source of conflict, the marsh dwellers refused fresh levies, and the provincial government had few troops to spare while it was committed elsewhere against Persia. The identity of the first movers and the course of events are variously reported and cannot be cited from any reliable source.
impact: 最直接的後果落在奴役體制上。津芝之亂被後世視為大批東非奴隸輸入伊拉克的終點：此後南方沼澤的農業仍需勞力，但役使形式改變，學者多認為自十世紀起黑奴不再成批用於土地生產，而多轉到家內服務與其他較分散的僱傭形式，這一轉變直接影響了阿拔斯晚期社會的勞動結構。政治上，中央為此耗去大量軍費與財力，延誤了對薩法里與拜占庭方向的用兵；穆瓦法克在戰後仍握實權，其子阿布·阿爾·阿巴斯於八八三年即位為穆塔迪德。思想上，這場以宗教改革與奴隸解放為號召的運動，被後世阿拉伯史家列為阿拔斯末期最酷烈的動亂之一，也成為主張最合格者當統治一類平等說法在伊斯蘭世界早期罕見的大規模實踐。軍事上，它留下一個典型教訓：正規騎兵在沒有道路的沼澤水網裡會被游擊隊分割。史料上，九世紀阿拉伯編年史與地理類著作對這十四年記載之詳細，在早期伊斯蘭史料中罕見其匹，成為研究南部鹽沼制度與地方軍隊的重要材料。此後數百年，南部沼澤的部族自治與中央徵稅之間的張力一直延續，一八二〇年代的騷動正是這條傳統的另一節。
impactEn: The most direct consequences fell on the system of slavery. The Zanj revolt came to be treated by later writers as the end of the large-scale import of East African slaves into Iraq: the southern marshes still needed labour, but the form of service changed, and scholars generally hold that from the tenth century black slaves were no longer used in bulk on the land but increasingly in household service and other more dispersed forms of employment, a shift that altered the labour structure of late Abbasid society. Politically the centre spent heavily in men and money and was delayed in its response to the Saffarids and to Byzantium; al-Muwaffaq still held real power after the war, and his son Abu al-'Abbas took the caliphate as al-Mu'tadid in 883. In the register of ideas, this movement, which carried religious reform and the emancipation of slaves in one, is ranked by later Arabic historians among the fiercest disturbances of the late Abbasid period, and it stands as one of the rare large-scale workings in the early Islamic world of the egalitarian claim that the most qualified man ought to rule. Militarily it left a standard lesson: regular cavalry loses cohesion when a roadless marsh and its canals are given to the raiders. For the historical record, the detail with which ninth-century Arabic chronicles and geographical works describe these fourteen years is hardly matched in early Islamic sources, and they remain a principal source for the institutions of the southern salt marshes and for provincial military life. For the centuries afterwards, the tension between tribal autonomy in the southern marshes and the taxation of the centre never went away, and the disturbances of the 1820s are another episode in that long line.
result: 八八三年八月，長期圍城與招撫之後，穆赫塔拉陷落，阿里·本·穆罕默德的下落在史料中有戰死與被擒兩說，較可靠的一說是他被自己人出賣後遭擒獲，首級被插在矛上，置於船隻沿運河往返示眾；餘部或降或散，戰役以哈里發軍獲勝告終，中央重新控制薩瓦德的鹽沼農業區與巴士拉以南的水道。十一月三十日阿布·阿爾·阿巴斯進入巴格達，舉行凱旋遊行並再次展示首級，作為對都城的震懾。據記載首腦被押往巴格達後處決，同批被殺的起義首領數十人；大量奴隸在戰後被重新編入政府軍隊與莊園，南部鹽沼的勞役制度也隨之重新編排。一八二〇年代那一線只知結局是南部沼澤的騷動被平定，省府以討伐與安撫並用的辦法收編部分部族、把沼澤納入常設稅收與駐軍體系，細節記載有限。就本卡而言必須講明：火繩槍在此役以及那一線的戰場上都沒有出現，它屬於槍械譜系裡十六世紀的一段，而本卡的戰爭記載跨越的年代遠在其前；方陣的彈幕要靠點火、瞄準與排隊，而南部鹽沼真正決定勝負的，是水道、舟隊、夜間的縱火，以及十四年裡誰能先把糧道接上。
resultEn: In August 883, after the long siege and the offers of pardon, al-Mukhtarah fell. The sources differ on whether Ali ibn Muhammad was killed in the fighting or taken alive, and the better supported account is that he was betrayed by one of his own and captured; his head was then impaled on a lance, set on a boat and carried up and down the canals for all to see. The rest either surrendered or scattered, the war ended in victory for the caliphal army, and the centre regained the Sawad salt-marsh plantations and the waterways south of Basra. On 30 November 883 Abu al-'Abbas entered Baghdad and held a victory parade in which the head was shown again, as a demonstration to the capital. According to the accounts the leader was taken to Baghdad and executed, with a number of chiefs, said to be several dozen, killed at the same time; large numbers of slaves were drawn back into government troops and estates, and the labour arrangements of the southern salt marshes were reorganised. For the 1820s thread only the outcome is known: the disturbances in the southern marshes were settled, and the provincial government used pursuit and accommodation together, taking in some of the tribes and bringing the marshes under regular taxation and a standing garrison, and the details of that process are thinly recorded. For this card one point must be stated plainly: the matchlock musket appeared on neither of these battlefields. It belongs to the sixteenth-century stretch of the firearms line, and the years covered by this war are far earlier. The volley of the square depends on lighting, aiming and rank, whereas what decided the fighting in the southern salt marshes was water, boats, fire carried in the dark, and which side could first keep a supply line open across fourteen years.
